name: Arab National Bank
legal_name: Arab National Bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 1979 (took over the Saudi operations of Arab Bank; listed on Tadawul 1 Dec 1979 per AR 2025)
ownership_summary: Listed Saudi bank with a foreign strategic shareholder. Arab Bank PLC (Jordan) held 800,000,000 shares (40.00%) at both 1 Jan and 31 Dec 2025, unchanged during the year. Other holders above 5%: Rashed Abdul Rahman Al-Rashed and Sons Co. (10.00%) and Al-Jabr Investment Co. (5.65%) (AR 2025 Directors' Report). The FS describe the capital as 60% Saudi and non-strategic foreign shareholders and 40% 'Strategic shareholder - Arab Bank PLC – Jordan'. Arab Bank PLC appoints 3 of the 10 directors; the other 7 are elected by shareholders.

shareholders.holder: Rashed Abdul Rahman Al-Rashed and Sons Co.

government_link: No government shareholder above 5% disclosed at 31 Dec 2025 (S3). One director is Chief Operating Officer of Hassana Investment Company (S2); no Hassana holding is disclosed.
group_structure: Parent bank with: anb capital (100%; CMA-licensed investment arm for brokerage, asset management, investment banking, real estate and private equity funds; profiled separately as sa-anb-capital); Al Arabi Heavy Equipment Lease Company (87.5%; board approved its sale on 23 Nov 2025, classified held for sale and discontinued at 31 Dec 2025); Al-Manzil Al-Mubarak Real Estate Financing Ltd. (100%; holds title to financed real estate); associate SHL Finance Company (29.4%; equity-accounted). International branch in London (35 Curzon Street, Mayfair). Double counting: anb capital is fully consolidated and reported as the 'Investment and brokerage services' segment (FY2025 total operating income SAR 556.3m, equal to anb capital's own SAR 556.2m). Do not add sa-anb-capital figures to this record.

footprint: Saudi Arabia plus one branch in London. At end-2025: 121 domestic branches (Central 44, Western 30, Eastern 27, Southern 20), 54 TeleMoney remittance centres, 14 SME centres, 3 corporate service centres and about 1,028 ATMs (AR 2025, S3). The Eastern Region hosts the bank's first Wealth Management Center (opened 2025).
customer_segments: Retail (mass, youth, expatriates, senior executives, women), affluent tiers (anb Silver, Gold, Platinum), anb Elite (launched 2025 for ultra-high-net-worth individuals), Private Banking (HNW, 'anb Private'), MSME, mid-sized corporates, corporate and institutional (Wholesale Bank Group), fintechs (transaction banking).
business_lines: Five reporting segments (FY2025 FS note 31): Retail banking (deposit, credit and investment products for individuals; total operating income SAR 3,782m), Corporate banking (SAR 4,259m), Treasury (SAR 1,425m), Investment and brokerage services (anb capital; SAR 556m), Other. Private Banking and the London branch sit inside the bank. Treasury sells structured deposits (AMLP), hedging and international bonds/sukuk, and runs the eTrader FX and precious-metals platform. TeleMoney remittances. Islamic Banking Division: Islamic assets nearly 90% of total assets and Islamic liabilities almost 99% of total liabilities at end-2025.

capabilities.wealth_summary: anb runs wealth through a tiered retail model (anb Silver, Gold and Platinum, with published entry deposits of SAR 100,000, 500,000 and 1,000,000), anb Elite (launched 2025 for ultra-high-net-worth clients) and Private Banking ('anb Private', a dedicated HNW branch plus the London branch for UK property and mortgages). In 2025 it opened what it calls the Kingdom's first Wealth Management Center in the Eastern Region and launched a female HNW programme. Investment products come from the 100%-owned anb capital (AUM SAR 24.6bn NAV at end-2025, 24 real estate funds, about 20 public funds, DPM from SAR 20m), which is small inside the group: the investment and brokerage segment was 5.6% of FY2025 operating income. The revamped anb app is 'integrated with anb capital' for investment products and fund subscriptions, while trading runs in anb capital's own apps. Treasury sells AMLP structured deposits, international bonds/sukuk, structured credit and hedge-fund exposure. The 2026 plan targets stronger affluent propositions, AI-driven personalisation, and at anb capital new investment lines with fintech partners.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking (anb Private) serves HNW clients through RMs, a dedicated HNW branch and the London branch (35 Curzon Street, reopened Q1 2025; UK mortgages extended to more cities and to other GCC clients). Offer: 'packages of products, services, and investment opportunities', investment planning, access to 'the Saudi and Global Markets', treasury products (swaps, hedging, Murabaha), 'structure customized investments', concierge via partners. 2025: revenue growth, more clients, 'higher assets under management' (no figures), female HNW programme. Strategy: 'start specialized programs targeting under-served HNWI segments and position the Bank as a multi-generational partner'.

asset_management.detail: Through anb capital (100%): AUM SAR 24.56bn net asset value and SAR 28.02bn gross asset value at 31 Dec 2025 (2024: 15.6bn / 20.4bn). Shariah and conventional public funds (Saudi equity, IPO, dividends, digital & IT, multi-asset, trade/money-market, sovereign sukuk, US and Asian equity), private fixed income funds, 24 real estate funds, PE/VC funds. Details in sa-anb-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through anb capital: Saudi Exchange plus GCC, Egypt and US markets (and other global markets via the Central Trading Unit); 'anb capital - Saudi' app, 'anb capital - Global' platform, IVR and phone brokers; conventional and Shariah margin lending. Brokerage value traded SAR 68bn in 2025; net brokerage income SAR 36m (-22%).

digital_investing.detail: The anb mobile app (revamped 2025) is 'integrated with anb capital to have access to an array of investment products' (AR 2025), and anb capital lists 'Easy subscription through anb mobile application' for its funds. Equity trading, IPOs and margin run in anb capital's separate apps (new Saudi trading app 2025; anb capital - Global with US fractional shares). Bank-run eTrader platform for FX and precious-metals trading (web and mobile). Third-party summaries mention a robo-advisory service and digital gold wallet, but these were not found on anb's website or in AR 2025.

advisory.detail: RM-led advice in Private Banking and Elite. 2025-2026 retail strategy: 'Affluent focus: Enhancing wealth advisory services, introducing dedicated affluent services'. anb capital Wealth Management offers research-driven advice and customised portfolios.

discretionary.detail: anb capital Discretionary Portfolio Management for corporate, institutional and HNW clients with investable assets of SAR 20m and above. DPM fees SAR 26.1m in FY2025.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on anb.com.sa, the anb capital website or in AR 2025. Third-party (Quartr) summaries of anb investor presentations mention a robo-advisory launch; not verified. anb capital public multi-asset funds (conservative, balanced, growth) act as risk-profiled fund options.

funds_platform.detail: anb capital's own funds are subscribed through the anb mobile app. No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: Treasury: anb Market Linked Structured Deposit Product (AMLP) linked to rates, FX or commodities with 'partial or full capital guaranteed' (business banking page). International Instruments page: structured products, structured credit, international bonds and sukuk in all major currencies, hedge funds (fund of funds, single managers). Private Banking: 'structure customized investments'. Issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: Via anb capital: 24 active real estate funds (7 launched in 2025), four PE/VC funds including the anb Seed Fund (10 fintech investments) and a 2025 healthcare fund (Baraya Extended Care). Treasury lists hedge-fund exposure. Elite clients get 'property investments' through anb capital.

islamic_wealth.detail: Islamic Banking Division under a Shariah Committee: Islamic assets nearly 90% of total assets at end-2025. Shariah products include Islamic time deposits with advance profit payment and ZAD time deposits ('a zakat-paid Sukuk-based product'), Shariah margin lending and Shariah funds at anb capital.

Revamped anb mobile app integrated with anb capital investment products; 60-second account opening; retail internet banking rebuilt with in-house hosting
Private Banking launched a dedicated female HNW programme; London branch reopened refurbished Mayfair offices (Q1 2025)
Launched the first bank-led fintech accelerator (anb Innovate) with Fintech Saudi; 16 fintechs selected; anb capital's anb Seed Fund participated

2026 goals (AR 2025): strengthen the affluent banking proposition; AI-driven personalisation and refined segmentation for high-value customers; at anb capital, 'Advance digital and client platforms' and 'Expand product innovation by introducing new investment lines and partnering with fintechs'
EGM elected the board for 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2029; Chair and Vice Chair appointed 16 Apr 2026 after SAMA no-objection

opportunities: AR 2025 2026 goals for anb capital: 'Advance digital and client platforms to enhance accessibility, engagement and overall CX' and 'Expand product innovation by introducing new investment lines and partnering with fintechs' (S3 PDF p.23)

Retail strategy: 'Affluent focus: Enhancing wealth advisory services, introducing dedicated affluent services'; 2026 retail focus on AI-driven personalisation for high-value customers (S3 PDF pp.23, 31)
Private Banking plans 'specialized programs targeting under-served HNWI segments' and a multi-generational proposition (S3 PDF p.58)
Wealth is a small share of group income: investment and brokerage segment SAR 556m of SAR 9,883m operating income in FY2025 (5.6%) (S4 note 31)
No model portfolios, robo or third-party funds found in the anb app; the app offers anb capital funds only (S3, S21)
Arab Bank PLC's Deputy CEO for Retail Banking and Wealth Management and its CEO sit on anb's board (S2)
barriers: Investment licences sit in anb capital (CMA licence 07072-37), so an investment-product contract would likely be with the subsidiary (S3, S19)
In-house build tendency: retail internet banking rebuilt on 'a unified back office and in-house hosting' (S3 PDF p.40); anb capital launched its own new trading apps in 2025 (S23)
Islamic-weighted balance sheet (Islamic liabilities almost 99% of total); products for most clients need Shariah Committee approval (S3 PDF p.33)
incumbent_vendors: IBM Safer Payments (fraud), integrated by ejada Systems, live Mar 2025 (S17)

discrepancies.detail: Internal notes said IBM is an integrator at anb. IBM's 11 Mar 2025 release shows IBM supplied the IBM Safer Payments fraud software, and ejada Systems implemented and integrated it. No IBM wealth or investment work found.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded IBM as a fraud-prevention software vendor and ejada as integrator. IBM integrator role not supported.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 (as at 31 Dec 2025, published Mar 2026) lists Saleh Almahmoud as Chief Private Bank Officer with biography. The official executive page (18 executives, checked 12 Oct 2026) lists no private banking head; the Arabic page was under maintenance. No 2026 appointment or departure news found (English and Arabic role-based searches).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded with role_status 'Conflicting sources' (people pass X17). Unresolved.

open_items: anb IR 'financial statements' and 'investor presentations' pages showed 'under maintenance' on 12 Oct 2026, so the H1 2026 interim FS, investor presentation and segment data were not opened. 30 Jun 2026 balance-sheet figures come from the Pillar 3 CC2 table and H1 income from Argaam. Saudi Exchange pages were not used (403 in prior batches; not re-tried).
Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results not yet published as of 12 Oct 2026. Re-check late Oct 2026.
Current head of Private Banking unconfirmed (Saleh Almahmoud in AR 2025, absent from the official page).

Third-party (Quartr) summaries of anb investor presentations say anb launched a robo-advisory service and a digital gold wallet. Not found on anb.com.sa, anb capital's site or AR 2025; verify against the investor presentation once the IR page is back.
Private Banking and Elite eligibility thresholds and Private Banking AUM are not published.
LinkedIn profiles for the CEO, Chief Retail Bank Officer and Chief Digital Officer not found via search; one unofficial page for Khaled Alrashed was not used.
Which anb capital products are available inside the anb app (funds only, or also equities) is not documented in detail.

People pass X17 (12 Oct 2026): Chief Private Bank Officer Saleh Almahmoud is now 'Conflicting sources' (AR 2025 lists him; the 18-person official executive page does not); the Arabic executive page (anb.com.sa/ar) was 'under maintenance', so it could not be used as a second official listing. Confirm the private banking head before meetings.

Appointment dates are not published for any current anb executive other than the CEO (Tadawul filing) and the Chief Wholesale Bank Officer (anb capital AR); the Chief Digital Officer, Chief Information Officer and Chief Marketing and Customer Experience Officer have no biography on the official page or in AR 2025. The AR 2025 shows the Chief Treasury Officer as Dr. Zeyad Abanmay; Ahmed Alsourani's 2026 appointment has no announcement.

Blocked or unusable in this pass: IBS Intelligence article bylined by the CIO (HTTP 403; cited as search result only), 24fintech speaker page for the CIO (redirects to the event home page), Saudi Exchange company profile (HTTP 403), anb Arabic executive page (maintenance notice). The search tool declines name-based LinkedIn look-ups; the only LinkedIn match found in role-based searches was for the COO (S30).

The AR 2025 does not identify which three directors are appointed by Arab Bank PLC (only Mohammed Alghanamah's biography says he represents Arab Bank); the post-April 2026 board page lists Ahmed Samer Hamdi Al Zaeem in place of Alghanamah. Board members other than the Chair, Deputy Chairman, CEO and the two Arab Bank executives are not profiled in this file.
